subject.title: fix: harden aerith native hook relay recovery

question: Should lost Codex PreToolUse relay recovery ever render a no-op for loop-detection-only commands, and under what payload checks?
rationale: That choice trades native-tool availability during Gateway recovery against OpenClaw's approval boundary, and current source still has a timeout path that can lose the payload needed for the decision.

options.title: Preserve approval boundary first
options.body: Require every unavailable path to pass the raw payload and fail closed whenever core or plugin approval could apply, allowing no-op only for proven observation-only payloads.

options.title: Accept the no-op carveout
options.body: Maintainers can intentionally accept the availability tradeoff after the timeout gap, tests, docs, and live recovery proof are fixed.

options.title: Defer to canonical stale-relay work
options.body: Pause this PR if the canonical issue should be solved by a narrower refresh or re-registration design instead.

recommendation.title: Preserve approval boundary first
recommendation.body: Require every unavailable path to pass the raw payload and fail closed whenever core or plugin approval could apply, allowing no-op only for proven observation-only payloads.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the strongest recent history on the native hook fallback contract and reliability changes being adjusted here.
